sections.h2: Address, hours and what the office does
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds is in the courthouse at 111 S. Michigan Avenue, Saginaw, MI 48602. Staff work weekdays from 8:00 until a quarter to five, with holidays off. Call (989) 790-5270 to reach the counter, or send a fax to (989) 790-5278. Counter hours can shift, so a quick phone call before you drive downtown is cheap insurance.

The register is an elected keeper of every real property record in the county. The office maintains the index and holds the original subdivision plats, and cities and townships call on it for liber and page references. Drafting and legal questions are off the table. The quitclaim deed form page says so plainly, so line up an attorney or title agent to write your deed.

For context, the 2020 census put the county at 190,124 people and 85,953 housing units, with 8.7% of the units vacant and 70.5% of occupied homes lived in by their owners.

The recording charge is $30 a document under MCL 600.2567, however many pages it runs. An assignment or discharge that reaches several instruments picks up $3 per extra instrument. The rest of the fee schedule looks like this:

  • Page copies at $1, with a $5 certification per document.
  • Counter searches at $5 apiece.
  • A free public workstation inside the office.
  • Tax certification, which the County Treasurer handles.

The counter takes cash, check, money order, American Express, Discover, Mastercard or Visa, and card payments add a fee. The Treasurer's certificate costs $5 for the first five parcel descriptions, then $1 more per description. Before you stand in line at the register, stop at the Treasurer in Room 107 to learn whether your instrument needs one.

The county posts a long checklist built on Michigan's recording statutes. Each line carries a statute number, and a paper that fails any of them may come back unrecorded. The lines below apply to deeds signed after April 1, 1997.

Saginaw County recording checklist
RequirementWhat the checklist asks for
Paper and typeWhite paper of at least 20 pounds, legible, in 10-point type or larger
Page sizeAt least 8.5 by 11 inches and no larger than 8.5 by 14
Margins2.5 inches clear at the top of page one and half an inch on every other side
Title lineFirst line names the single recordable event the paper evidences
SignaturesOriginal, in black or dark blue ink, with the name printed beneath
Notary blockDated acknowledgment, printed notary name and commission expiration
Legal descriptionPlat caption and lot number, or quarter section, section, town and range if unplatted

More lines follow. A street or post office address for the grantee is required, and so is the drafter's name and address. Anyone signing after September 12, 2017 must black out the first five digits of a Social Security number, and foreign-language text needs a translation stapled behind it.

sections.h2: Transfer tax on a Saginaw County deed
sections.html:
The checklist states a rate of $8.60 per $1,000 of consideration. Either the deed itself shows total consideration or a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit goes in with it. Where nothing is owed, the deed cites the exemption instead.

State law makes the seller responsible, with payment to the county treasurer inside 15 days of delivery (MCL 207.523). MCL 207.526 exempts a handful of transfers, among them a land contract that leaves title with the vendor, a boundary line adjustment with no payment, a mineral rights conveyance, and a spouse's conveyance that creates or ends a tenancy by the entirety.

Treat the transfer tax line as a closing cost you plan for, not a surprise. Your title company or closing attorney will usually calculate it from the contract price and deduct it from your proceeds. If you think your deal qualifies for an exemption, tell them before closing so the right statute gets cited on the deed.

A few papers need extra proof. If a deed names a survivor, the death certificate must be certified and either recorded separately or cited by liber and page. A court order arrives certified and sealed by the clerk. A release or assignment points back to the original liber and page or document number.

The sequence usually runs like this. The assessor values the parcel, the treasurer collects what is owed and certifies the status, and the register records the deed and indexes it for anyone searching later. A seller who knows which desk answers which question wastes less time. Michigan leaves assessing and building permits with cities and townships, so a Saginaw County buyer or seller often deals with three offices: the township or city assessor, the county treasurer and this register. Each has its own counter and its own phone number. Parcels also sit in one of about twenty school districts, so name the district in your listing.

sections.h2: What the Treasurer adds to a deed transfer
sections.html:
Tax questions go to Room 107 in the same courthouse, open weekdays from eight to five. That office takes over delinquent real property tax, manages the Delinquent Tax Revolving Fund, and its head chairs the Land Bank Authority that handles tax foreclosed parcels. Without the certificate, state law keeps most warranty deeds off the record (MCL 211.135).

Back taxes can be paid at the counter, mailed to 111 S. Michigan Avenue or paid on the web around the clock. The web payment runs through an outside vendor that adds an access fee on the total. A card payment that is later reversed voids the payment, and the fees and interest reapply back to the original date.

sections.h2: How a seller should prepare to file
sections.html:
Work through these steps in order:

  1. Look up the current deed and legal description on the office workstation.
  2. Learn from the Treasurer whether a certificate applies, and pay for it apart from recording.
  3. Show the price on the deed or prepare the valuation affidavit, and carry the tax payment.
  4. Compare margins, ink, notary block and grantee address with the checklist.
  5. Phone ahead about card fees and counter hours, and carry $30 per document.

After closing, the register passes transfers along to local assessors, and the buyer files a separate form with the assessor inside 45 days. Taxable value then resets to the state equalized value for the next year (MCL 211.27a). A cash buyer who closes quickly still needs every item above, because the checklist does not bend for speed. Paperwork prepared in advance is what lets a short closing stay short.

If the house is an inherited property, bring the certified death certificate and any court order so staff can see how the chain of title runs from the prior owner to you.

faqs.q: What does recording cost at the Saginaw office?
faqs.a: Thirty dollars a document, plus $3 for every extra instrument one document assigns or discharges. Copies run $1 a page and certification costs $5.
No. Staff cannot prepare documents or offer legal advice. The quitclaim deed page sells access to a blank form for $5 plus an access fee, and sends owners to an attorney for legal help.

faqs.q: How is the Saginaw County transfer tax stated?
faqs.a: The checklist gives $8.60 per $1,000 of consideration. Sellers owe it, and an exempt transfer cites its exemption on the instrument.
The Saginaw County Treasurer issues it, and the register does not. The fee is $5 for up to five descriptions and $1 per description past that.

faqs.q: What number do I call for the register?
faqs.a: Call (989) 790-5270. The office is in the courthouse at 111 S. Michigan Avenue, and faxes go to (989) 790-5278.
